tldr: Mem-α is a reinforcement learning framework that trains LLM agents to learn effective memory construction strategies for complex multi-component memory systems, using downstream question-answering accuracy as reward signal. Despite training exclusively on sequences up to 30k tokens, the agent generalizes to sequences exceeding 400k tokens.
contributions: Proposes Mem-α, a reinforcement learning framework that trains agents to effectively manage complex memory systems through interaction and feedback
Constructs a specialized training dataset of 562 balanced instances from MemoryAgentBench spanning conversations, document sharing, pattern recognition, and storytelling
Designs a three-component memory architecture (core, episodic, and semantic memory) with specialized tools for memory operations
Demonstrates significant improvements over existing memory-augmented agent baselines with strong generalization to sequences over 13× the training length
methods: The authors formulate memory construction as a sequential decision-making problem using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). The agent processes information chunks and decides which memory operations (insert, update, delete) to perform across a three-component memory architecture (core memory: max 512-token summary; semantic memory: structured factual statements; episodic memory: timestamped events). The reward signal combines four components: correctness reward (QA accuracy via a decoupled RAG pipeline), tool call format reward, compression reward (1 - l_m/l_c), and memory content reward (validated by Qwen3-32b). Training uses 562 instances sampled from MemoryAgentBench with Qwen3-4B as backbone, trained on 32 H100 GPUs for 205 steps.
results: Mem-α achieves significant improvements over baselines (Long-Context, RAG-Top2, MemAgent, MEM1) across Accurate Retrieval, Test-Time Learning, and Long-Range Understanding tasks. Ablation studies show RL provides substantial gains beyond the memory structure alone. The approach reduces memory footprint by approximately 50% compared to Long-Context and RAG-Top2 baselines. The method generalizes to sequences exceeding 400k tokens (up to 474K in Multi-Doc dataset), over 13× the maximum training length of 30k tokens.
limitations: Trained exclusively on instances with maximum length of 30k tokens and averaging under 20k tokens; generalization to 400k+ tokens is demonstrated but not trained directly on such lengths
Conflict Resolution dimension is excluded from evaluation due to lack of realistic benchmarks, as existing datasets remain predominantly synthetic
Memory content reward requires Qwen3-32b for validation, adding computational overhead
The four reward hyperparameters (β=0.05, γ=1 fixed) require tuning, and their effect on different configurations is shown separately rather than being principled
